headline: Adjusted earnings and guidance rise despite GAAP profit dip
summary_short: Revenue rose 23.0% y/y to $7.50B on the Calpine acquisition; GAAP EPS fell to $1.42 from $2.67 y/y even as Adjusted (non-GAAP) Operating EPS rose to $2.55 from $1.91, and full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised to $11.50-$12.50.
summary_long: Revenue was $7.50B, up 23.0% y/y but down 32.5% q/q as Q1's cold-weather demand normalized; Calpine's addition and favorable market/portfolio conditions lifted results, partially offset by nuclear outages. GAAP net income fell to $513M ($1.42/share) from $839M ($2.67/share) y/y, while Adjusted (non-GAAP) Operating Earnings rose to $920M ($2.55/share) from $599M ($1.91/share) -- the gap is mostly non-cash fair-value and Calpine commodity-contract amortization excluded from the adjusted figure. Operating income fell to $580M from $951M y/y as nuclear generation dipped to 44,160 GWh (93.0% capacity factor) on more refueling outage days (86 vs 41). Cash fell to $697M from $1,974M y/y after $2.5B of Calpine-related investing outflows and $2.0B of YTD buybacks. Full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance raised to $11.50-$12.50.

drivers.explanation: Adjusted (non-GAAP) Operating Earnings growth was driven mainly by the addition of Calpine and favorable market and portfolio conditions, tempered by unfavorable nuclear outages.

GAAP EPS fell despite higher adjusted earnings; a $340M unrealized fair-value loss and $149M non-cash Calpine commodity-contract amortization, both excluded from the adjusted figure, explain most of the gap.
Nuclear output fell to 44,160 GWh from 45,170 GWh y/y as planned refueling outage days rose to 86 from 41, pressuring results ahead of Calpine's contribution.
